column1: # Partition table for the P1 board -- replaces Arduino's default.csv.
# WHY. The stock table gives the application 1280K and then parks 1408K in a
# SPIFFS partition this firmware never opens: the web pages are compiled into the
# binary as PROGMEM strings and every setting lives in NVS. A third of the chip
# was doing nothing while the app slot sat at 95% full.
# WHAT CHANGED. app0/app1 grow 1280K -> 1856K each
column2: and what is left of the dead

column1: # SPIFFS space becomes a small LittleFS partition. Two app slots are kept
# still works: the running image is never the one being overwritten.
# NVS IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED
column2: same offset and same size as the stock table.

column1: # That is what makes this change safe to apply to a board already in service --
# calibration
# settings all survive. Move nvs by one byte and every one of them is gone.
# THE 256K littlefs is for telemetry that could not be delivered: with MQTT to
# ThingsBoard
column2: a dropped link would otherwise be a hole in the history. Roughly
400 records of (timestamp + V/I/P/Hz + 9 temperatures) at ~48 bytes each

column1: # which is about 3.7 days of outage buffered at one record a minute. It is only
# written to while the link is down
column2: so flash wear is a non-issue.

column1: # FLASHING. A table change cannot be delivered over OTA -- OTA writes app slots
# not the table at 0x8000. The first flash after this must go over USB:
#     pio run -e web_dashboard -t upload
# OTA works normally from then on.
# Offsets are exact: app partitions are 64K-aligned as the bootloader requires
# and the last byte of coredump is the last byte of a 4MB chip.
#   0x00e000  otadata     8K
#   0x3b0000  spiffs    256K   (formatted LittleFS -- see below)
#   0x3f0000  coredump   64K   -> 0x400000 = 4MB exactly
# THE DATA PARTITION IS NAMED "spiffs" ON PURPOSE
# LittleFS volume. Arduino's LittleFS.begin() defaults to the partition labelled
# "spiffs"
column2: and so does PlatformIO's uploadfs -- name it "littlefs" instead and

column1: # both quietly fail to find it
column2: plus the IDF tool warns that the label collides
